title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is handwritten on the back of a Bourbaki typescript; the faint typed text is the Haar-measure draft n°370, as on the neighbouring pages. That draft has nothing to do with the content.

(1) Top lines, continuing a lost previous sheet. Grothendieck guesses there should exist a smooth projective X over a number field k and two embeddings v, v' : k -> C such that H*(X_v, Z) and H*(X_{v'}, Z) are not isomorphic as RINGS. 'On devrait mettre Serre à contribution' points to Serre's 1964 Comptes Rendus note on conjugate projective varieties that are not homeomorphic; there the fundamental groups differ. The margin asks: 'Peut-on remplacer Z par R??', i.e. could even the real cohomology algebras differ?

In modern terms: H*_dR(X/k) is one k-algebra, and its base changes along v and v' are the complex cohomology algebras. Étale comparison gives H*(X_v, Z_l) = H*_et(X_kbar, Z_l) = H*(X_{v'}, Z_l) for every l. So the obstruction to a ring isomorphism is genuinely global and integral or real.

(2) Main paragraph, reconstructed in modern terms:
- Let k be a number field, v0 : k -> C an embedding, and M a motive over k.
- The Betti fibre functor at v0 on the tensor category generated by M, with its Z-lattice, gives a Tannakian group G_{M,v0} = Aut^⊗(ω_{v0}), which Grothendieck insists is 'défini sur Z'.
- Any other embedding v gives a second fibre functor ω_v, hence a torsor ('fibré principal homogène') P_v = Isom^⊗(ω_{v0}, ω_v) under G_{v0}.
- Conjecture A: if M is 'assez compliqué', then v ≠ v' implies P_v is not isomorphic to P_{v'}. The integral Betti torsor would remember the embedding.
- A bolder version (reading 'Plus hardi' for the transcribed 'Plus haut') seems to ask, for M general enough, that the relevant torsors P under G_{v0} come from embeddings v. This is a surjectivity statement.
- He then defines π^1_M(k, v) := G_{M,v}(Z), a discrete arithmetic group of finite type, and calls it the 'vrai groupe fondamental' (reading uncertain).

The link with part (1) is implicit but exact. Cup product is a morphism of motives h(X)⊗h(X) -> h(X). So a trivialisation of P_v over Z (resp. over R) yields a ring isomorphism H*(X_{v0}, Z) = H*(X_v, Z) (resp. with R). Hence non-isomorphic cohomology rings certify nontriviality of the torsor, and the margin question is whether P_v can already be nontrivial over R. Over C it is always trivial, since fibre functors over an algebraically closed field are isomorphic.

By Artin's comparison, P_v is trivial over every Z_l. So its class lies in an everywhere-locally-trivial, genus-type subset of H^1(Z, G). This is consistent with the finiteness of the set of embeddings. Grothendieck does not say this explicitly; it is part of my reconstruction.

(3) Left margin: requiring a functorial isomorphism ξ(M)⊗_Z C = M_σ⊗_k C, with ξ the integral Betti functor and M_σ the de Rham realisation, compatible with Riemann–Hodge type conditions, 'risks being a very serious condition'. This is a worry about defining motives with integral structure as systems of realisations with comparison isomorphisms and polarisations.
errors: As literally stated, Conjecture A is false for v' equal to the complex conjugate of v. Complex conjugation gives a homeomorphism X_v(C) -> X_{v'}(C), compatible with all motivic morphisms. Hence there is a canonical tensor isomorphism ω_v = ω_{c∘v} and P_v = P_{cv}. The conjecture must be read for archimedean places (embeddings up to conjugation), or 'v' already means a place.

A Tannakian group 'défini sur Z' is not given by the formalism over a field: lattices of Betti realisations do not form an abelian category, and flatness and representability need justification (cf. later work on Tannakian duality over Dedekind and valuation rings). The phrase is a programme, not a construction.

Calling G_M(Z) finitely generated and arithmetic presupposes that G_M ⊗ Q is a linear algebraic group (e.g. reductive for pure motives), which is conjectural. For an Artin motive one gets a finite Galois group, which is consistent with the name 'fundamental group'.
The existence of the Z-cohomology-ring counterexample is only conjectured here. Serre's 1964 examples differ in π1, not visibly in cohomology rings.

ideas.what: Expectation of conjugate smooth projective varieties with non-isomorphic integral cohomology rings, and the question whether even real cohomology algebras can differ
ideas.modern_name: Conjugate varieties with distinct cohomology algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (1964, non-homeomorphic conjugates via π1); Abelson (1974, homotopy-distinct conjugates); F. Charles (2009, 'Conjugate varieties with distinct real cohomology algebras', Crelle), which answers the R-question positively

ideas.what: Motivic Galois group of M taken with respect to the Betti fibre functor at an embedding, with an integral structure
ideas.modern_name: Integral motivic Galois group / Mumford–Tate-type group scheme over Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (motivic Galois group idea, 1960s), Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne–Milne (1982); integral versions much later and partial
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via Saavedra's thesis and Récoltes et Semailles; the integral version is not published

ideas.what: Each embedding v gives a torsor P_v = Isom^⊗(ω_{v0}, ω_v) under the motivic Galois group; Conjecture A says these torsors separate embeddings for sufficiently complicated M; a bolder variant asks that torsors come from embeddings
ideas.modern_name: Torsors of fibre functors attached to conjugation; cf. Taniyama group and conjugation of Shimura varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Langlands (1979), Deligne ('Motifs et groupes de Taniyama', 1982), Milne–Shih — over Q and A_f for CM motives; no integral 'separation' conjecture known to me

ideas.what: π^1_M(k, v) := G_{M,v}(Z), a discrete arithmetic group proposed as the 'true fundamental group' attached to a motive
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic subgroup of the motivic Galois group (no established notion)

ideas.what: Defining motives with an integral Betti functor plus a comparison ξ(M)⊗C = M_dR⊗_{k,σ}C subject to Riemann–Hodge (polarisation) conditions, with the worry that this is a serious restriction
ideas.modern_name: Motives as systems of realisations with comparison isomorphisms (Deligne 1979, Jannsen 1990); integral period structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, Jannsen; Fontaine for p-adic analogues

missed.claim: Grothendieck links the existence of conjugate varieties with non-isomorphic Z- or R-cohomology rings to the nontriviality of the Betti torsors P_v over Z or R. This turns Serre-type conjugate counterexamples into statements about classes in H^1(Z, G_M) and H^1(R, G_M) of the motivic Galois group. He asked in 1965 exactly the question that F. Charles answered in 2009 (real cohomology algebras can differ).
missed.quote: H^*(X_v, Z) et H^*(X_{v'}, Z) non isomorphes comme anneaux ... Peut-on remplacer Z par R??
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Charles's examples, and later work on conjugate varieties, can be read as computing nontrivial motivic torsor classes. The torsor viewpoint suggests systematically classifying conjugates via (everywhere-locally-trivial) H^1 of integral motivic Galois groups.

missed.claim: Conjecture A: for sufficiently complicated M, distinct embeddings (necessarily up to complex conjugation) give non-isomorphic integral Betti torsors under G_M. A bolder variant appears to ask that the relevant torsors all arise from embeddings. Since these torsors are trivial at all Z_l (étale comparison), this would identify archimedean places with part of a genus-type class set of G_M over Z.
missed.quote: conjecture A : si M est assez compliqué, v ≠ v' ⇒ P_v ≠ P_{v'}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An integral, Betti-theoretic recovery of the embeddings of k from a single motive is a kind of anabelian/Tannakian reconstruction. It is not formulated in the literature as far as I know, and could be tested on abelian varieties with explicit Mumford–Tate groups.

missed.claim: The proposal that the integer points of the integral motivic Galois group, G_M(Z), form a discrete finitely generated 'true fundamental group' π^1_M(k, v) attached to k, v and M.
missed.quote: G_{M v}(Z) = π^1_M(k,v) un groupe ... discret. ... groupe fondamental
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: There is no standard notion of a discrete arithmetic 'motivic fundamental group' of this type. It would sit between Mumford–Tate arithmetic groups (monodromy, period domains) and Galois groups.

deep.surprise_reason: The page anticipates, in 1965, both the question resolved by Charles (2009) on real cohomology algebras of conjugate varieties and a torsor-theoretic framework over Z linking embeddings to classes of motivic Galois torsors. The framework is close in spirit to the later Taniyama-group and conjugation-of-Shimura-varieties theory, but integral, with an unpublished separation conjecture. It is fragmentary and partly mis-stated (complex conjugation), so it falls short of a genuine finished result.
transcription_corrections: Margin 'Peut-on remplacer Z par R??' sits at the top left beside the cohomology-ring question, so it refers to H*(X_v, Z) versus H*(X_v, R).
'Plus haut' is more plausibly 'Plus hardi' (bolder), introducing a stronger conjecture.
'conjecture' is written above a struck-out word ('dite' or similar) before 'A'.
'un groupe à générateurs en nombre fini [?] (arithmétiques [?]) discret' likely reads 'un groupe à générateurs et relations en nombre fini (arithmétique) discret'.
The page is written on the verso of a Bourbaki typescript (n°370, Haar measure). The neighbouring 'pages' are typescript rectos and unrelated to the manuscript content.
The subscript in 'G_{M v_Z}(Z)' is probably G_{M,v}(Z) or G_{M,v_0}(Z).
